Implication for you: this isn't a reason to change GOOG's stop or avoid new momentum entries, but it's a reason to keep respecting stop-limits strictly and not let cash sit un-deployed out of complacency once SPXC clears.

📚 Today you learned

Buffett Indicator Part 3 — Why Two Sources Can Disagree by 60 Points

Today's macro card showed 237.9% from one source and 301% from another — same indicator, same day, wildly different numbers. The formula is simple (total market cap ÷ GDP), but GDP is a quarterly, backward-looking government estimate while market cap updates every second. A site using the latest official GDP print (usually 1-2 quarters stale) will read lower than one extrapolating GDP forward to "today." Neither is wrong — they're measuring the same ratio with a different denominator lag. The practical rule: trust the trend direction and the zone (both agree we're in "all-time extreme" territory) more than the precise number, and always check which GDP vintage a source is using before comparing two readings. This is the same lesson as trusting IBKR over search for SPXC's price today — a stale or extrapolated input can look precise and still be wrong.

Also today: GDP nowcasting — statistical models (like the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow) that estimate the current quarter's GDP in real time before official data is released, which is what feeds the higher "301%" style readings.
